This vignette is a compact smoke test of the package's three operating-model
examples. It runs each model with smaller spatial grids or sample sizes so the
examples remain quick to render. Every plotted result is a **ggplot2** object.

## Winker et al. (2014) cluster example

The cluster simulator represents trips that visit two of four habitats. This
example checks that it returns the expected trip data and that all diagnostic
plots are ggplot objects.

```{r cluster-simulation}
cluster <- simulate_cluster(
  years = 6,
  trips_per_year = 40,
  seed = 101
)

cluster_plots <- plot_cluster_2014(cluster)

stopifnot(
  nrow(cluster$data) == 6 * 40,
  all(c("biomass", "effort", "catches") %in% names(cluster_plots)),
  all(vapply(cluster_plots, inherits, logical(1), "ggplot"))
)
```

```{r cluster-effort-plot}
cluster_plots$effort
```

## Four-species bathymetric Run 22 example

This is the four-species spatial model. Habitat association is bathymetric;
there is no vertical-availability component in this scenario.

```{r bathymetric-simulation}
bathy_settings <- bathymetric_settings()
bathy_settings$n_years <- 4
bathy_settings$Nvessels <- 4
bathy_settings$Tot_effort <- 35
bathy_settings$Range_X <- 1:10
bathy_settings$Range_Y <- 1:10
bathy_settings$SpatialScale <- 2

bathymetric <- simulate_bathymetric(bathy_settings, seed = 202)

stopifnot(
  all(c("Data", "Biomass", "Biomass.XY", "Plots") %in% names(bathymetric)),
  all(c("Depth", "SpDens", "Hist", "CPUE") %in% names(bathymetric$Plots)),
  all(vapply(bathymetric$Plots, inherits, logical(1), "ggplot"))
)
```

```{r bathymetric-density-plot}
bathymetric$Plots$SpDens
```

## Tuna spatial and vertical example

The tuna model adds a vertical dimension: species depth profiles are shifted
by a thermocline anomaly field and hook depths follow the catenary model of
Bigelow et al. (2002) for each HBF. Here we use a small grid and check the
returned diagnostics and the vertical-profile plot.

```{r tuna-simulation}
tuna_cfg <- tuna_settings()
tuna_cfg$n_years <- 4
tuna_cfg$nx <- 10
tuna_cfg$ny <- 10
tuna_cfg$n_vessels <- 4
tuna_cfg$effort <- 60

tuna <- simulate_tuna(tuna_cfg, seed = 303)
vertical_plot <- plot_tuna_vertical_distributions(tuna_cfg)

stopifnot(
  all(c("Data", "Biomass", "Plots") %in% names(tuna)),
  all(c("HBF", "hook_depth", "vertical_avail", "hbs_avail") %in% names(tuna$Data)),
  all(vapply(tuna$Plots, inherits, logical(1), "ggplot")),
  inherits(vertical_plot, "ggplot")
)
```

```{r tuna-vertical-plot}
vertical_plot
```

## Reproducibility

Each simulation call receives a seed, so the example is reproducible. The
small settings used here are for testing and illustration; use the default
settings or a calibrated scenario for substantive simulation experiments.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
